annotation_description: Cast Seam Rip without first making their land drop. With a third land (Island or Hallowed Fountain from hand), they would have had 3 mana available and could have cast both Seam Rip (W) AND Voice of Victory (1W) this turn, deploying a very powerful creature that prevents opponent from casting spells during their turn while also removing a threat.

Bouncing Voice of Victory instead of Seam Rip is suboptimal. Seam Rip is exiling one of Kimi's permanents (likely the Otter Token from Stormchaser's Talent, which is no longer on the battlefield). Bouncing Seam Rip would both remove the enchantment from play AND return the exiled permanent to Kimi's battlefield, creating a 2-for-1. Voice of Victory can simply be replayed next turn by the opponent.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: Floodpits Drowner's ETB trigger taps a creature and puts a stun counter on it. The choices include Toph, Hardheaded Teacher (a 3/4 creature that generates value by earthbending lands into creatures whenever spells are cast) and Spirebluff Canal (a land, which is only a valid target because Toph likely earthbent it into a creature). Tapping Toph and putting a stun counter on it would neutralize the opponent's most threatening creature for at least a full turn cycle, preventing it from attacking and blocking. Additionally, Floodpits Drowner has the activated ability to shuffle itself and a creature with a stun counter into their owners' libraries, which could permanently remove Toph. Instead, targeting Spirebluff Canal (a land-creature likely with just a +1/+1 counter) wastes the stun on a much less impactful target.

High Noon on the stack would lock MiMo Romance to one spell per turn, which is devastating with 7 cards in hand at 3 life. MiMo needs to deploy multiple threats quickly to close out the game. Three Steps Ahead can cleanly counter High Noon for 3 mana, which MiMo has available.

High Noon restricts each player to one spell per turn. MiMo Romance has 7 cards in hand including multiple creatures, Ajani, and interaction pieces that they need to deploy rapidly at 3 life. Allowing High Noon to resolve means they can only cast one spell per turn, making it nearly impossible to stabilize with their full hand. They had Three Steps Ahead and exactly enough mana ({1}{U}{U} from Island, Hallowed Fountain, Starting Town) to counter it.

MiMo Romance missed lethal. Opponent is at 2 life with only Toph (3/4) as a blocker. Casting the second Floodpits Drowner from hand (cost {1}{U}) would tap Toph via ETB and put a stun counter on it, allowing the existing Floodpits Drowner (2/1) to attack unblocked for exactly lethal.
